hooks.text: A tiny moon is the whitest world in the Solar System.
Which moon acts like a giant snow machine for Saturn's rings?
This frozen ball of ice is actually spraying hot water into space.

title: The Moon That Acts Like a Snow Machine
description: Enceladus is the most reflective body in the Solar System, and its massive water geysers actually create one of Saturn's rings.

beats.text: A tiny moon is the whitest world in the Solar System.
beats.visual: Enceladus natural color full disk mosaic, Cassini spacecraft, 2005

beats.text: Enceladus reflects nearly 100 percent of the sunlight hitting its frozen shell.
beats.visual: close up of Enceladus's bright icy surface, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: Astronomer William Herschel first spotted this 500-kilometer ice ball back in 1789.
Its extreme brightness comes from a gravitational tug-of-war with Saturn and the moon Dione.
beats.visual: diagram of Enceladus and Dione orbiting Saturn

beats.text: This tidal flexing generates enough internal heat to melt a global ocean beneath the ice.
beats.visual: cross-section illustration of Enceladus showing internal ocean and rocky core

beats.text: In 2005, the Cassini spacecraft discovered massive geysers erupting from fractures called tiger stripes.
beats.visual: Enceladus tiger stripes fractures close-up, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: These plumes spray ice and organic molecules directly into space to build Saturn’s E ring.
beats.visual: Enceladus water plumes backlit by the Sun, Cassini mission, 2005

beats.text: Most of that material eventually falls back as fresh snow.
beats.visual: artist concept of snow falling on the surface of Enceladus

beats.text: That is why a tiny moon is the whitest world in the Solar System.
beats.visual: distant view of Enceladus within Saturn's E ring, Cassini mission, 2006

better_than_last: I used the 'record' structure to highlight Enceladus as the most reflective body before explaining the mechanics of its geysers and ring formation.
